scenarios.name: Optimistic (single generalist, sustained focus, no rework)
Most likely (realistic single-resource throughput incl. overhead/context-switching)

input.nonLabourLines: [{"description": "Stripe integration / payment gateway fees and sandbox testing", "amount": 500}, {"description": "Third-party services: transactional email provider, search/indexing service, FX rate feed subscription", "amount": 1500}, {"description": "Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (build agents, staging environment hosting) for project duration", "amount": 2000}, {"description": "Observability/tracing tooling (APM, dashboards) subscription", "amount": 1200}, {"description": "Accessibility audit tooling / external WCAG audit", "amount": 1500}, {"description": "Legacy data migration tooling / temporary DB compute for Oracle extract", "amount": 2500}], "type": "array"}]
assumptions: The provided rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: there is only one generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr, 1 FTE, with no differentiation between frontend, backend, QA, DevOps, PM, etc. All costs below are therefore indicative only and should be revisited once real roles and rates are assigned to team members.

With only 1 FTE available, all 24 backlog items (total 189 story points) must be delivered sequentially by a single generalist. This is a major capacity risk: a team of this size would typically need 6-12+ months of calendar time to absorb this backlog, and true parallel work streams (e.g. concurrent frontend/backend/infra work) are not possible.

Story points were converted to hours using an approximate 8 hours/point baseline for a generalist doing analysis, build, test, and basic deployment, then adjusted per task for known complexity (e.g. legacy migration, payment integration, RBAC) - this is a rough heuristic, not derived from historical velocity.
No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project yet; estimate is a bottom-up judgment estimate only and carries wide uncertainty until real data is collected.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 400k customers / 2M invoice lines from Oracle) and Payment provider integration (PW-7) are treated as the highest-risk, highest-effort items given data volume and financial/compliance sensitivity, and are allocated proportionally more hours than raw story points might suggest.

Non-labour costs assume modest cloud/SaaS tooling spend typical for a small project (CI/staging infra, email/search/FX vendors, APM/observability, accessibility audit, temporary migration compute) - actual vendor selection and contracts are not yet known.
Priority breakdown allocates each task's full labour cost to its stated priority bucket; tasks with the same priority are assumed to consume effort roughly proportional to their story points.

Given 1 FTE, calendar duration will be materially longer than a typical multi-role team; this estimate reflects effort/cost only, not elapsed time, and elapsed time should be modeled separately once staffing is clarified.

Assumed a standard 5-day, 8-hour working pattern with no overtime premium; the $75/hr rate is applied uniformly to all hours regardless of task type (design, build, test, ops) since only one role exists on the rate card.
input.reasoning: "Total backlog is 189 story points across 24 tasks. Because the only staffed role is a single generic 'Team member' at $75/hr with 1 FTE, I modeled effort in hours per task using an approximate 8 hours/story-point baseline, then applied multipliers for tasks with disproportionate real-world effort relative to story points (e.g., PW-8 legacy migration is very data/risk heavy relative to its 21 points; PW-7 payment integration carries compliance/reconciliation complexity; PW-4 RBAC and PW-3 auth carry security-critical testing overhead). This produced a most-likely total of ~2,160 hours (~$162,000 labour) for a single resource, which at 1 FTE (approx. 2,000 productive hours/year after PTO/overhead) represents roughly 12-13 months of continuous work - a critical staffing risk given the backlog size and mix of urgent/high priority items. I added optimistic (-25%) and pessimistic (+30%) scenarios to reflect the wide uncertainty inherent in a single-generalist delivery model, unclear task complexity, and lack of historical velocity data. Non-labour costs were estimated separately for typical SaaS/tooling/infrastructure needs implied by the backlog (CI/staging, Stripe, email, search, FX feed, observability, accessibility audit, migration compute) since these are real costs independent of the placeholder rate card. Priority totals were computed by summing each task's estimated labour cost into its stated priority bucket, showing that Urgent+High priority items alone account for the majority of the budget and should be protected from descoping."

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 pts) to a later phase; support staff can use direct DB/read-only tooling in the interim.
reductions.effect: Removes an entire feature area from this phase; support agents temporarily rely on manual/read-only workarounds until a later release.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low priority, 8 pts) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 pts) to a post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: No analytics dashboards or automated helpdesk contract tests at launch; finance reporting done manually, helpdesk integration risk monitored manually instead.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-15 (Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA) scope to critical customer-facing flows only rather than all screens for initial release.
reductions.effect: Full AA compliance across all screens deferred; risk of accessibility complaints/legal exposure on lower-traffic admin screens until follow-up pass.

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal, Low priority, 8 pts) until after the new portal has been live and stable for a full billing cycle.
reductions.effect: Legacy portal and its infrastructure continue running (with associated hosting cost) slightly longer, but reduces risk of premature cutover.

reductions.description: Simplify PW-14 (Multi-currency support) to launch with USD only and add EUR/PLN in a fast-follow release.
reductions.effect: Initial launch only supports single currency; multi-currency invoicing/FX handling delivered in a subsequent phase.

reductions.description: Re-scope PW-8 (Legacy data migration) to migrate only active/recent records at cutover, archiving the remainder for on-demand migration.
reductions.effect: Reduces migration engineering and validation effort significantly; a small number of dormant accounts may need manual/late migration on request.

reductions.description: Given only 1 FTE is currently staffed against a 189-point backlog, strongly recommend confirming real roles/rates and adding capacity before committing to the full most-likely estimate; every deferred low-priority item above reduces schedule risk more than it reduces raw dollar cost, since the real constraint is throughput, not budget.
reductions.effect: No direct dollar saving, but materially de-risks delivery timeline; should be treated as a precondition for the estimate above being achievable within a reasonable calendar window.
